 Indiana State Police are investigatign four deaths at a West Lafayette home. The coroner has identified all four victims, including two teenage girls.

 Indiana State Police are investigating the deaths of four people found inside a West Lafayette home Wednesday night. Authorities responded to a 911 call in the 1300 block of Shining Armour Lane on November 18. The Tippecanoe County Coroner’s Office identified the deceased as Thomas Tkach, 51…

 "Thirty-two, was a shooter at home? It was going to be the caller's father. She advised that her father had a gun and was threatening to shoot the family. I heard multiple gunshot go off and the line is now silent," a audio recording from 9-1-1 dispatch said. 
 A 9-1-1 call Wednesday night led police to a West Lafayette home, where investigators report they found four people dead. Two of them were teenagers. Just after 8:30 p.m., deputies and officers responded to the 1300 block of Shining Armour Lane.
 Four people have been found dead, including two juveniles. Right now, investigators are working to determine exactly to see what happened as the community waits for answers.
 Indiana state police say there's no ongoing threat to the public but questions remain about what led to these deaths.
 The Tippecanoe county coroner’s office has now identified all four victims:
 51-year-old Thomas Tkach, 53-year-old Julie Tkach, 17-year-old Katharyn Tkach, and 16-year-old Lauren Tkach.
 Thomas Tkach worked as a jail deputy with the Tippecanoe County Sheriff’s Office. In a news release, the sheriff's office confirmed Tkach had taken the role July 14, 2024. He later worked in a courthouse security position beginning in February 2025. He did not have disciplinary action taken against him.
 Meanwhile, Katharyn and Lauren were listed on Harrison High School’s flag football roster and Julie Tkach was an assistant professor i n hospitality and tourism management  at Purdue University. 
 Investigators have not confirmed how the four died or exactly how they are related.
 Autopsies are scheduled for Friday as authorities continue working to determine what happened here.
